champion: Florid cutaneous papillomatosis with urothelial cancer
ordered_diagnoses: Florid cutaneous papillomatosis with urothelial cancer
Paraneoplastic syndrome with transitional cell carcinoma

s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of oral and cutaneous lesions with abdominal discomfort and difficulty eating, associated with a large renal mass and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Sudden warty growths over the lips
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in the axillae, posterior neck, periumbilical region, and groin folds
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms with papillomatous appearance
key_facts: 70-year-old woman
Sudden onset of oral lesions
Difficulty eating
6-month history of vague abdominal discomfort
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in multiple areas
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms
Large left-sided renal mass with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy on abdominal CT
Necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy causing superior vena cava compression on thorax CT
Invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation on radiologically guided biopsy of renal mass

shortlist.label: Florid cutaneous papillomatosis with urothelial cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of sudden onset oral and cutaneous lesions with abdominal discomfort and difficulty eating, associated with a large renal mass and lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Invasive renal urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Radiologically guided biopsy of renal mass revealed invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation favoring a urothelial primary

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic syndrome with transitional cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Association between the renal mass and the cutaneous lesions suggests a paraneoplastic syndrome

shortlist.label: Acanthosis nigricans
shortlist.why_kept: Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in multiple areas are consistent with acanthosis nigricans, a paraneoplastic syndrome

shortlist.label: Tripe palms
shortlist.why_kept: Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms are consistent with tripe palms, a paraneoplastic syndrome

s4.champion: Florid cutaneous papillomatosis with urothelial cancer

raw.champion: Florid cutaneous papillomatosis with urothelial cancer
raw.rationale: The patient's sudden onset of oral lesions, extensive papillomatosis, and characteristic palm lesions are consistent with florid cutaneous papillomatosis, which is often associated with internal malignancies, in this case, the large left-sided renal mass with invasive carcinoma.

rejected.label: Invasive renal urothelial carcinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a renal mass with invasive carcinoma, this option does not fully explain the cutaneous manifestations.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic syndrome with transitional cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This option is close but less specific to the cutaneous findings described.

rejected.label: Acanthosis nigricans
rejected.why: This condition can present with velvety skin lesions but does not fully account for the oral and palm findings.

rejected.label: Tripe palms
rejected.why: This is a feature of the patient's presentation but not a comprehensive diagnosis for the entire clinical picture.
